creative_extensions.claim_text: KULR's proprietary cooling solutions have been developed through longstanding partnerships with NASA, the Jet Propulsion Lab and others, and KULR's CTO Dr. Walker worked at NASA Johnson Space Center 2
creative_extensions.source_label: NASA TechPort
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: https://techport.nasa.gov/api/projects/search?searchQuery=KULR
creative_extensions.rationale: NASA TechPort indexes every NASA-funded technology project with partner organizations. A real 'longstanding NASA partnership' should produce one or more TechPort project entries listing KULR as principal investigator or commercial partner.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: list of NASA TechPort project IDs with KULR as partner + project title + funding amount + center (JSC/JPL)
creative_extensions.signal_direction: if 0 TechPort projects name KULR as commercial partner over 2018-2024, contradicts 'longstanding NASA partnership' framing

creative_extensions.claim_text: KULR's proprietary cooling solutions have been developed through longstanding partnerships with NASA, the Jet Propulsion Lab and others, and KULR's CTO Dr. Walker worked at NASA Johnson Space Center 2
creative_extensions.source_label: NASA NTRS (Technical Reports Server)
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/search?q=KULR
creative_extensions.rationale: NASA technical reports / conference papers co-authored with commercial partners are indexed in NTRS. CTO Walker's NASA-JSC publications and any KULR-NASA co-authored reports would appear here.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: count of NTRS citations naming KULR + Walker's pre-2022 NASA publications + any post-2022 NASA-KULR joint reports
creative_extensions.signal_direction: presence of NASA-KULR co-authored reports corroborates partnership; pure 'Walker worked at NASA before joining KULR' without joint output post-2022 weakens 'longstanding partnership' framing

creative_extensions.claim_text: KULR's proprietary cooling solutions have been developed through longstanding partnerships with NASA, the Jet Propulsion Lab and others, and KULR's CTO Dr. Walker worked at NASA Johnson Space Center 2
creative_extensions.source_label: NASA SBIR/STTR Award Database
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: https://sbir.nasa.gov/api/awards?firm=KULR
creative_extensions.rationale: NASA SBIR/STTR awards are the canonical small-business-NASA partnership vehicle. Companies with 'longstanding NASA partnership' generally have multiple Phase I/II awards.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: count of NASA SBIR/STTR awards, phase, dollar value, topic
creative_extensions.signal_direction: 0 NASA SBIR awards while claiming longstanding partnership = contradiction signal

creative_extensions.claim_text: KULR's solutions target high-performance applications in direct energy, hypersonic vehicles and satellite communications for aerospace and Department of Defense applications.
creative_extensions.source_label: SAM.gov entity NAICS + business types
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: sam_entity.query_entity_by_uei (after UEI resolved from usaspending)
creative_extensions.rationale: SAM declares the entity's primary NAICS + business-type flags (small-disadvantaged, woman-owned, defense-related). A DoD-supplier claim implies primary NAICS in 3364/3345/3328 family. If SAM primary is 335991 (Primary Battery Mfg) or 334513, that's consistent. If SAM primary is 541330 (Engineering Services) only, that's weaker.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: primary_naics, business_types, exclusion_status, registration_active
creative_extensions.signal_direction: NAICS-vs-claim scope contradiction if primary NAICS doesn't include any defense/manufacturing family

creative_extensions.claim_text: KULR's solutions target high-performance applications in direct energy, hypersonic vehicles and satellite communications for aerospace and Department of Defense applications.
creative_extensions.source_label: DoD SBIR/STTR (DSIP) award database
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: https://www.dodsbirsttr.mil/topics-app/api/awards?company=KULR
creative_extensions.rationale: Direct-energy, hypersonic, and satcom work commonly enters DoD via AFRL/Navy/MDA SBIR. DSIP indexes these by company.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: count of DSIP awards, agency (AFRL/MDA/Navy), topic title, dollar value, phase
creative_extensions.signal_direction: 0 DSIP awards with 'hypersonic vehicles' or 'satcom' or 'directed energy' topics while claiming DoD applications in those domains = inflation signal

creative_extensions.claim_text: KULR's solutions target high-performance applications in direct energy, hypersonic vehicles and satellite communications for aerospace and Department of Defense applications.
creative_extensions.source_label: MDA / Space Force / AFRL public press releases
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: site:mda.mil OR site:spaceforce.mil OR site:afrl.af.mil 'KULR' (archive.org snapshots pre-2025-05-15)
creative_extensions.rationale: DoD program offices announce contractor selections publicly. Hypersonic + direct-energy + satcom announcements that involve KULR would be archived.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: count of mda/sf/afrl press releases naming KULR pre-cutoff
creative_extensions.signal_direction: 0 mentions across these three program offices while claiming all three domains = strong inflation signal

creative_extensions.claim_text: KULR holds a portfolio of granted U.S. patents covering carbon-fiber thermal management materials, lithium-ion battery thermal runaway mitigation, and the Fractional Thermal Runaway Calorimeter (exclu
creative_extensions.source_label: USPTO PatentsView assignee disambiguated lookup
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: https://search.patentsview.org/api/v1/patent/?q={"assignees.assignee_organization":"KULR"}
creative_extensions.rationale: PatentsView disambiguates assignee variants (KULR vs KULR Technology vs KULR Technology Group vs KULR Technology Corporation) — useful when patents are filed under operating-subsidiary names that differ from corporate brand.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: list of patents with normalized assignee, priority date, classification (CPC subclass H01M for batteries / F28F for heat exchangers)
creative_extensions.signal_direction: if PatentsView returns 0 patents but uspto_odp returns some (or vice versa), the disambiguation gap is informative; absolute count <5 across both is weak for a 12-year-old company claiming 'proprietary core technology'

creative_extensions.claim_text: KULR holds a portfolio of granted U.S. patents covering carbon-fiber thermal management materials, lithium-ion battery thermal runaway mitigation, and the Fractional Thermal Runaway Calorimeter (exclu
creative_extensions.source_label: USPTO Patent Assignment Database (PAS)
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: https://assignment.uspto.gov/patent/index.html (assignee=KULR)
creative_extensions.rationale: The April 2023 'exclusive license to commercialize the patented Fractional Thermal Runaway Calorimeter' implies a recorded assignment or license. PAS records public assignment/license transactions. The licensor (NREL? a university? an inventor?) and any post-license re-assignment activity would appear here.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: license/assignment record showing licensor name + patent numbers covered + execution date matching 'April 2023'
creative_extensions.signal_direction: absence of any recorded assignment/license to KULR pre-cutoff matching the FTRC patent family contradicts the 'exclusive license' claim

creative_extensions.claim_text: KULR holds a portfolio of granted U.S. patents covering carbon-fiber thermal management materials, lithium-ion battery thermal runaway mitigation, and the Fractional Thermal Runaway Calorimeter (exclu
creative_extensions.source_label: NREL FTRC patent family
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: Google Scholar / NREL.gov search 'fractional thermal runaway calorimeter' + USPTO assignee=NREL or Alliance for Sustainable Energy
creative_extensions.rationale: The 'Fractional Thermal Runaway Calorimeter' was developed at NREL by Walker et al. The licensor in KULR's April 2023 license is almost certainly NREL / Alliance for Sustainable Energy LLC (DOE M&O contractor). Cross-checking the underlying patent family against KULR's claimed exclusivity is the most direct verification.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: list of FTRC patents originally assigned to NREL / Alliance for Sustainable Energy; license-status flag on the DOE Lab Partnering Service
creative_extensions.signal_direction: if patents are non-exclusively licensed to multiple companies, contradicts 'exclusive license' framing; if no FTRC patent family exists, contradicts the whole 'patented' claim

creative_extensions.claim_text: KULR maintains battery design, cell testing, battery production, and battery storage & transportation operations from a principal executive office at 555 Forge River Road, Suite 100, Webster, Texas 77
creative_extensions.source_label: EPA FRS (Facility Registry Service) reverse-lookup at Webster TX
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: epa_emissions.query_facility_emissions with company_name='KULR' and claimed_locations=[{city:'Webster',state:'TX'}]
creative_extensions.rationale: Battery production + cell testing involves electrolytes, solvents, and lithium handling — these processes typically trigger EPA permits (RCRA generator status, air-quality, stormwater). FRS reverse-lookup at the Webster TX address tests whether ANY entity is EPA-permitted there. CALIBRATION CAVEAT (Heuristic H1): small-cap pre-revenue battery shops often operate below regulatory thresholds; absence is moderate, not severe.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: list of FRS-registered facilities at 555 Forge River Rd or matching company_name='KULR' anywhere in TX
creative_extensions.signal_direction: presence at Webster TX corroborates real industrial ops; absence is moderate (could be sub-threshold lab-scale prototyping)

creative_extensions.claim_text: KULR maintains battery design, cell testing, battery production, and battery storage & transportation operations from a principal executive office at 555 Forge River Road, Suite 100, Webster, Texas 77
creative_extensions.source_label: Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) Central Registry
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: https://www2.tceq.texas.gov/crpub/index.cfm?fuseaction=regent.RNSearch (regulated entity search by city=Webster)
creative_extensions.rationale: TCEQ regulates Texas-specific air, water, and waste permits at lower thresholds than federal EPA FRS. Battery production with solvents triggers TCEQ air permits. State-level registry catches operations below EPA-FRS threshold.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: TCEQ Regulated Entity (RN) and Customer (CN) numbers for KULR; permits issued (air, waste); inspection history
creative_extensions.signal_direction: TCEQ permit history at 555 Forge River corroborates production claim; total absence weakens 'battery production' framing toward 'design + testing only'

creative_extensions.claim_text: KULR maintains battery design, cell testing, battery production, and battery storage & transportation operations from a principal executive office at 555 Forge River Road, Suite 100, Webster, Texas 77
creative_extensions.source_label: Harris County Appraisal District (HCAD) parcel records
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: https://hcad.org/property-search/ (address=555 Forge River Rd, Webster TX) — note Webster is in Harris County, TX
creative_extensions.rationale: County assessor records show parcel ownership, building square footage, improvement type (office vs warehouse vs industrial), and improvement year. A claimed 'principal executive office' with 'battery production' should show industrial/flex sqft, not just office sqft. Lease vs ownership also visible.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: parcel-level building type, total sqft, improvement description (office/warehouse/manufacturing/flex)
creative_extensions.signal_direction: if building is pure-office (<5000 sqft office-only), inconsistent with 'battery production' operations; if flex/industrial sqft is meaningful, consistent

creative_extensions.claim_text: KULR maintains battery design, cell testing, battery production, and battery storage & transportation operations from a principal executive office at 555 Forge River Road, Suite 100, Webster, Texas 77
creative_extensions.source_label: DOL H-1B LCA filings at the Webster TX worksite
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: dol_h1b_lca.query_lca_filings with employer_name='KULR' and city='Webster' and state='TX'
creative_extensions.rationale: KULR's CTO came from NASA-JSC (Houston area, ~20 miles from Webster). Battery / thermal engineers often require advanced degrees — sub-20-emp tech operations frequently file LCAs.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: count of certified LCAs at Webster TX, SOC codes (engineering/materials science), worksite address validation
creative_extensions.signal_direction: presence corroborates engineering-team-at-Webster claim; absence is moderate (small US-citizen-only teams file 0 LCAs)

creative_extensions.claim_text: KULR allocated approximately $65M to Bitcoin treasury (217.18 BTC at $96,696 in Dec 2024; additional 449.45 BTC at $99,008 by March 27, 2025; total 666.63 BTC valued at $58.1M on March 27, 2025) and e
creative_extensions.source_label: On-chain Bitcoin treasury wallet verification
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: blockchain explorer (mempool.space / blockstream.info) — if KULR has published a treasury address or proof-of-reserves
creative_extensions.rationale: Per claim, KULR holds 666.63 BTC ($58.1M) on Coinbase Custody. Some BTC-treasury small-caps publish treasury wallet addresses (proof-of-reserves) — MSTR-style transparency. If KULR has published an address, on-chain balance vs claimed balance is direct.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: wallet balance matching 666.63 BTC at March 27, 2025 snapshot
creative_extensions.signal_direction: absence of published address means the claim is auditor-attested only (Marcum); reconciliation via 10-K/10-Q balance sheet across quarters is the only continuing test

creative_extensions.claim_text: KULR allocated approximately $65M to Bitcoin treasury (217.18 BTC at $96,696 in Dec 2024; additional 449.45 BTC at $99,008 by March 27, 2025; total 666.63 BTC valued at $58.1M on March 27, 2025) and e
creative_extensions.source_label: SEC Form 8-K filings for Bitcoin purchases
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: sec_filings.list_filings_by_form with cik='0001662684', forms=['8-K'], start_date='2024-12-01', cutoff_date='2025-05-15'
creative_extensions.rationale: Material Bitcoin purchases by public companies (MSTR pattern) typically trigger 8-K Item 8.01 disclosures. 217 BTC at $21M and 449 BTC at $44M are material to a sub-$200M-revenue company. 8-K cadence verifies the timeline.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: count and dates of 8-Ks mentioning Bitcoin between Dec 2024 and May 2025; alignment with claimed Dec 22 and Q1 2025 purchase dates
creative_extensions.signal_direction: no 8-Ks for material BTC purchases would be a disclosure failure; presence + matching dates corroborates

creative_extensions.claim_text: KULR allocated approximately $65M to Bitcoin treasury (217.18 BTC at $96,696 in Dec 2024; additional 449.45 BTC at $99,008 by March 27, 2025; total 666.63 BTC valued at $58.1M on March 27, 2025) and e
creative_extensions.source_label: MSTR-clone screen: BTC-per-share / NAV-premium dilution dynamics
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: Computed: BTC holdings ($58M) + cash ($25M) = $83M crypto-treasury vs market cap at 2025-05-15; ATM proceeds ($60M in 2024, $51M Q1 2025) split between operations vs Bitcoin
creative_extensions.rationale: KULR is a 'BTC-treasury micro-cap' archetype: small operating business + Bitcoin as primary treasury asset + perpetual ATM funding the BTC stack. The pattern (MSTR-clone at micro-cap scale) typically requires sustained BTC price appreciation to generate per-share BTC accretion; if BTC declines while ATM dilution continues, BTC-per-share goes negative — distress signal. This isn't directly externally adjudicable but is a structural framing that informs claim_evolution interpretation.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: ratio of (BTC value + cash) to market cap; ATM cumulative shares issued vs total shares outstanding; BTC-per-share trajectory
creative_extensions.signal_direction: if (BTC + cash) approaches or exceeds market cap, suggests market discounts core business to ~$0 — distress signal

creative_extensions.claim_text: KULR allocated approximately $65M to Bitcoin treasury (217.18 BTC at $96,696 in Dec 2024; additional 449.45 BTC at $99,008 by March 27, 2025; total 666.63 BTC valued at $58.1M on March 27, 2025) and e
creative_extensions.source_label: Bitcoin mining lease counterparty identification
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: Search EDGAR fulltext for KULR mining-lease counterparty (the 'bitcoin mining services company' is unnamed in the filing slice — full 10-K + 8-K may identify the counterparty); cross-check counterparty's own 10-K / 10-Q for the 2,500 S-19 lease
creative_extensions.rationale: A 2,500-miner S-19 fleet at $850K for 60 days implies the lessor operates a real Bitcoin mining facility with hosting capacity. Major US mining hosts (Core Scientific, Riot, CleanSpark, Marathon, Hut 8) all file 10-Ks. If the counterparty is a public miner, their disclosures may confirm or contradict the lease.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: counterparty name; confirmation in counterparty filings; hosting capacity consistency
creative_extensions.signal_direction: if no named counterparty and 8-K omits identification, weaker disclosure quality; if named and counterparty doesn't disclose lease in their own filings (sub-material), expected — true sub-material; if named counterparty disputes existence, contradiction

creative_extensions.claim_text: KULR raised approximately $111M via ATM equity offerings between July 2024 and March 27, 2025 ($60.13M net in 2024 plus $51.12M gross in Jan-Mar 2025) against a 2024 revenue base of $10.7M and net los
creative_extensions.source_label: ATM prospectus supplements (424B5) cadence
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: edgar_fts.query_fulltext with search_term='At the Market', cik='0001662684'
creative_extensions.rationale: ATM upsizings each require 424B5 prospectus supplement filings. The filing cadence directly mirrors dilution velocity. KULR upsized ATM from $20M to $46M (Dec 4, 2024) then added another $50M (Jan 24, 2025) — three upsizings in ~7 weeks is a high-velocity dilution pattern.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: count of 424B5 filings between July 2024 and May 2025 + dates of upsizing 8-Ks
creative_extensions.signal_direction: 3+ upsizings within 12 months is high-velocity dilution; cluster with declining stock price = death-spiral signal

creative_extensions.claim_text: KULR raised approximately $111M via ATM equity offerings between July 2024 and March 27, 2025 ($60.13M net in 2024 plus $51.12M gross in Jan-Mar 2025) against a 2024 revenue base of $10.7M and net los
creative_extensions.source_label: Share count trajectory (diluted shares outstanding by quarter)
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: Parse 10-Q cover-page diluted-share counts for Q1-Q4 2024 + Q1 2025; compute (end - start) / start dilution rate
creative_extensions.rationale: ATM at $51M Q1 2025 alone issued 19.4M new shares — material vs prior share count. A high single-quarter dilution rate + perpetual ATM at falling price is the canonical micro-cap distress pattern.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: diluted shares outstanding by quarter; cumulative dilution YoY
creative_extensions.signal_direction: >50% YoY dilution + falling stock price = SEVERE distress signal

creative_extensions.claim_text: During 2024 KULR took at least three merchant cash advances with annualized effective interest rates of 86%, 217%, 240% and 249% (secured by accounts receivable), totaling roughly $2.96M in obligation
creative_extensions.source_label: Merchant cash advance lender identification + UCC liens
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: Texas Secretary of State UCC filings search (debtor='KULR Technology Corporation' or 'KULR Technology Group') — https://direct.sos.state.tx.us/ucc/
creative_extensions.rationale: Merchant cash advances secured by accounts receivable typically file UCC-1 financing statements at the debtor's state of organization. UCC search by debtor reveals: (a) lender names, (b) collateral descriptions, (c) liens still active vs terminated. The lenders' identity (predatory specialty MCA shops vs mainstream lenders) is itself diagnostic.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: list of UCC-1 filings naming KULR as debtor, with secured party + collateral description; UCC-3 terminations confirming repayment
creative_extensions.signal_direction: presence of multiple UCC-1s from known MCA shops (Reliant Funding, Yellowstone Capital, etc.) corroborates predatory funding pattern; presence of liens still active despite claimed repayment = contradiction

creative_extensions.claim_text: During 2024 KULR took at least three merchant cash advances with annualized effective interest rates of 86%, 217%, 240% and 249% (secured by accounts receivable), totaling roughly $2.96M in obligation
creative_extensions.source_label: MCA usage pattern across other distressed micro-caps
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: edgar_fts.query_fulltext with search_term='merchant cash advance' across all 10-K filers — establish base rate
creative_extensions.rationale: Public companies disclosing merchant cash advances at 200%+ APRs is exceptionally rare and usually concentrated in cash-strapped sub-$50M-revenue issuers (cf. legacy meme micro-caps). Establishing the base rate quantifies how distressed KULR's borrowing channel is.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: count of 10-K filers disclosing MCA usage over 2020-2024; revenue-decile distribution
creative_extensions.signal_direction: if KULR is in the top decile of MCA-dependent disclosure, that's a quantified distress percentile

creative_extensions.claim_text: KULR reported record annual revenues of $10.7M for 2024 compared to $9.8M for 2023 (9% YoY growth), while net loss was $17.5M in 2024 vs $23.7M in 2023.
creative_extensions.source_label: Operational capacity reality-check against revenue claim
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: Cross-check OSHA Form 300A headcount (KULR-4 result), DOL H-1B LCA workforce (KULR-4 result), and EPA/TCEQ permit profile against $10.7M revenue base
creative_extensions.rationale: A real battery-engineering services + production business at $10.7M revenue should have ~20-50 employees (industry benchmark: ~$200-500K revenue per technical employee in low-volume battery prototyping). If OSHA/LCA/permits suggest much less operational fingerprint, possible revenue concentration in non-recurring service contracts or related-party transactions.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: headcount + facility footprint consistency with $10.7M revenue scale
creative_extensions.signal_direction: operational fingerprint << implied scale = inflation / one-time-revenue signal

creative_extensions.claim_text: KULR reported record annual revenues of $10.7M for 2024 compared to $9.8M for 2023 (9% YoY growth), while net loss was $17.5M in 2024 vs $23.7M in 2023.
creative_extensions.source_label: Customer concentration in 10-K Note (sub-segment of revenue claim)
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: Full 10-K Note on Revenue / Customer Concentration — typically discloses customers >10% of revenue and federal-vs-commercial split
creative_extensions.rationale: $10.7M revenue is small enough that 1-2 large customers can drive YoY growth. If 'record revenue' is concentrated in DoD/NASA contracts, KULR-1 and KULR-2 federal-presence checks will corroborate. If concentrated in unnamed commercial customers, more concerning.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: customer concentration table with top customers + % of revenue
creative_extensions.signal_direction: high concentration on a few customers + KULR-2 INFLATION_SUSPECT signal would compound concern

creative_extensions.claim_text: KULR has commercial offerings including 'trigger cells' and 'TRS' (Thermal Runaway Shield) product sales, plus safety testing services and the K1-DS platform for custom energy storage solutions, with
creative_extensions.source_label: DOT/PHMSA Special Permits for lithium battery shipment containers
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: https://www.phmsa.dot.gov/approvals-and-permits/hazmat/special-permits-search (party='KULR')
creative_extensions.rationale: KULR's 'TRS' (Thermal Runaway Shield) and battery-transportation packaging products would commonly be deployed under DOT/PHMSA special permits for Class 9 lithium battery shipments. Companies that manufacture certified Li-ion shipping containers typically hold or are named on PHMSA special permits.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: PHMSA special permits naming KULR as grantee, manufacturer, or party-in-interest; permit subject (Class 9 lithium battery containers)
creative_extensions.signal_direction: presence of PHMSA permits corroborates real shipping-container business; absence is weak signal (KULR could be supplier-of-record, not permit-holder)

creative_extensions.claim_text: KULR has commercial offerings including 'trigger cells' and 'TRS' (Thermal Runaway Shield) product sales, plus safety testing services and the K1-DS platform for custom energy storage solutions, with
creative_extensions.source_label: FAA Cargo regulations / SAFO compliance for damaged battery transport
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: FAA Hazardous Materials Safety database + DOT incident reports for lithium battery shipping incidents naming KULR products
creative_extensions.rationale: FAA regulates Li-ion cargo transport on aircraft. KULR's product positioning includes 'transport and recycling packaging' — products in commercial use should leave a regulatory trail (FAA Form 5800.1 hazmat incident reports either using or testing KULR packaging).
creative_extensions.expected_observable: FAA hazmat incident records mentioning KULR-branded packaging; FAA approvals/qualifications
creative_extensions.signal_direction: presence of recorded FAA hazmat compliance corroborates real commercial deployment; absence is weak (products tested at lab scale may not generate FAA records)

creative_extensions.claim_text: KULR has commercial offerings including 'trigger cells' and 'TRS' (Thermal Runaway Shield) product sales, plus safety testing services and the K1-DS platform for custom energy storage solutions, with
creative_extensions.source_label: NIST battery-safety standards bodies + IEC 62133 / UL 2580 certification listings
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: UL Product iQ database (https://iq.ulprospector.com/) search 'KULR'; NIST Energy Storage Test Pad publications
creative_extensions.rationale: Battery-safety products typically need UL certification to be sold commercially. UL Product iQ indexes certified products by manufacturer. NIST publishes battery-safety reference standards; participants in standards-setting work would appear in NIST workshop attendee lists.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: UL-certified products listing KULR as mfr; NIST workshop participation
creative_extensions.signal_direction: absence of UL listings while claiming commercial Li-ion safety products is moderate contradiction; presence is corroboration

creative_extensions.claim_text: KULR has commercial offerings including 'trigger cells' and 'TRS' (Thermal Runaway Shield) product sales, plus safety testing services and the K1-DS platform for custom energy storage solutions, with
creative_extensions.source_label: TAM source quality audit
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: Internal review — Precedence Research / Market and Markets Research / CoherentMI are paid TAM-vendor reports; cross-check claims against authoritative sources (DOE, BloombergNEF, BNEF Battery Outlook)
creative_extensions.rationale: Citing 'private space exploration market $1.1T by 2030' from CoherentMI is a TAM-inflation signal — CoherentMI is a low-rigor market-research aggregator. BNEF / IEA / DOE projections are typically 5-10x lower. TAM-source quality is itself diagnostic of management's marketing tendencies.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: comparison of CoherentMI projection vs IEA/DOE 2030 space-economy figures
creative_extensions.signal_direction: TAM cited from low-rigor source while ignoring authoritative source = marketing-inflation signal
